1.why: I remember basic algebra from high school but lack recent practice to feel confident solving these problems now.

2.why: Working with decimals is tricky for me as I find them less intuitive than whole numbers or fractions.

3.why: Geometry concepts are not my strongest and I struggle with visualizing angles without a diagram.

4.why: Algebra problems often trip me up because I prefer literature and creative subjects over abstract math.

5.why: Trigonometry is very abstract and I have almost no memory of it from my past education.

6.why: Calculating area and volume is basic enough for me to attempt but I lack confidence in doing it correctly.

7.why: Sketching curves requires advanced graphing skills that I never developed and feel completely lost at.

8.why: Fractions are easier for me than decimals but I still avoid math tasks that require careful calculation.

9.why: Finding missing side lengths involves geometry rules I do not recall well and I find intimidating.

1.why: My dislike for math makes tables stressful but not panic-inducing like other math tasks.

2.why: Thinking about an upcoming test triggers significant worry given my history of hating maths.

3.why: Watching algebra on a blackboard is mildly uncomfortable but not overwhelming for me.

4.why: Taking a full math exam causes the worst bad feelings and high anxiety for me.

5.why: Difficult homework due soon creates quite a lot of anxiety and pressure for me.

6.why: Listening to a math lecture feels somewhat bad but I can usually manage it.

7.why: Hearing a student explain formulas is mildly uncomfortable but not too troubling for me.

8.why: Surprise pop quizzes in math class trigger quite a lot of anxiety and worry.

9.why: Starting a new math chapter feels fairly bad and moderately stressful for me.

1.why: I dislike maths and physics, but my high conscientiousness keeps me from feeling anxious about math ability.

2.why: I prefer computer science over math. I do not see myself as a naturally good math person.

3.why: Math is not a strength. I generally struggle to learn mathematical concepts quickly or effectively.

4.why: I am unsure about future math courses. My low agreeableness and stress make me hesitant about future expectations.

5.why: I find it hard to understand math content. My favorite subjects are CS and literature, not maths.

6.why: Getting an A in math is unlikely for me. I dislike the subject and lack confidence in that area.

7.why: I cannot do the mathematics required in a course. I prefer computer science and avoid math-heavy classes.

8.why: Test anxiety is moderate due to my dislike of math. I worry but not strongly because I avoid it.

9.why: Preparing for math tests is stressful. My high conscientiousness makes me try hard despite my lack of interest.

10.why: I get nervous but not excessively. I have low neuroticism, so extreme test anxiety is not typical.

11.why: Getting an A is unlikely. I worry a little but my low neuroticism prevents high levels of anxiety.

12.why: I worry about grades but not too much. My high conscientiousness helps me manage some stress levels.

13.why: I am not confident during tests. I dislike math and physics and prefer other subjects like CS.

14.why: I do not believe I can do well on tests. Math is not a strength for me at all.

15.why: Homework is stressful. My high conscientiousness makes me take it seriously despite my dislike of the subject.

16.why: I get nervous using math outside school. I prefer photography and gardening over real-world math applications.

17.why: I am not confident using math outside school. I dislike maths and lack confidence in my abilities.

18.why: I worry about career math. I prefer CS but worry my math skills are insufficient for future needs.

19.why: I worry I will not understand the math. My dislike of maths and physics makes comprehension difficult.

21.why: Listening to math instructors is stressful. I dislike math but my low neuroticism keeps anxiety manageable.
